title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation:  Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning regression and classification tools typically do not capture model uncertainty, whereas Bayesian models do but at prohibitive computational cost. The paper casts dropout training in neural networks as approximate variational inference in deep Gaussian processes, yielding MC dropout: averaging T stochastic forward passes to estimate predictive mean and variance. On UCI regression benchmarks, notably Boston Housing, MC dropout improves test RMSE and predictive log-likelihood over VI and probabilistic back-propagation, achieving 2.97 ± 0.19 RMSE on Boston Housing in the 20-split setting.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The authors' repo is cloned and contains the entire experimental apparatus: experiment.py, net/net.py, and all UCI_Datasets directories with data.txt, the exact 20 train/test index splits, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs/n_hidden configs, plus the authors' published result files (test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt etc.) for direct comparison. Nothing data- or weight-wise is missing (models are trained from scratch). What is broken is the runtime: the code targets Keras 2.2.0 on Theano 0.8.2 (README), Theano is unmaintained and not installable on Python 3.12, TF1.x/Keras 2.2 wheels do not exist for Python 3.12, and 9 of 11 Python files are Python-2 style. So we keep the authors' logic (architecture, dropout rates, epochs, tau/grid-search protocol, per-split train/val selection) but port the training/evaluation core to a modern framework and run the same splits.
est_runtime: Port work: ~20-30 min (rewrite net/net.py + experiment.py training/MC-dropout loop in a modern framework, keep split loading and grid-search logic). Runs (Boston Housing, 1x50 net, 400 epochs, batch 32, per-split grid over the repo's dropout_rates/tau_values, T MC forward passes): ~10-15 s per model fit on 22 CPU cores, so ~2-4 min per split with grid search. Full 20-split C1 protocol is ~40-80 min of compute, i.e. borderline-to-over the ~60 min total budget once the port is included.
scale_down_plan: Keep the exact released protocol but shrink along the split axis, not the model axis: evaluate the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits (index_train_*/index_test_*), same 1-hidden-layer/50-unit net, same dropout rates, same l=1e-2, same per-split train/val grid over tau, same 10x epochs (400), batch 32, Adam, T MC forward passes. Report mean test RMSE with standard error over 5 splits and state the split count explicitly. Secondary cheap confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308, <1 min/split) if time permits. Expected effect on the number: the point estimate should land near the released 2.83-2.97 range within a much wider error bar (SE roughly sqrt(20/5)~2x larger, i.e. +/-0.3-0.4 instead of +/-0.19); the qualitative claim (MC dropout beats VI, comparable-to-better than PBP 3.01) remains testable, but the printed +/-0.19 cannot be matched with 5 splits. If the port finishes fast, extend toward 10-20 splits; do not cut epochs or MC samples first, since those change the estimator itself.
blockers: code targets Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0; Theano is dead and cannot be installed on Python 3.12
Keras 2.2.0 / TensorFlow 1.x have no wheels for Python 3.12 (and Keras 3 API differs: layer-level train-time dropout loops, .compile/.fit behaviour, model saving)
9 of 11 python files are Python-2 style (print statements, old import style) and need 2to3-style edits even before framework porting
no GPU on this machine; README launch command assumes device=gpu + float32 (not fatal: the UCI nets are tiny and the paper reports CPU-class runtimes, e.g. naval 276 s/split incl. BO)
protocol requires a per-split train/val split + grid search over dropout rate and tau before the final train, so per-split cost is much larger than a single 400-epoch fit

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction: we keep the authors' released data and the exact 20 per-split train/test index files from https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps (bostonHousing/data/data.txt, index_train_i.txt, index_test_i.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt) and their grid-search-over-dropout-rate-and-tau protocol, but re-implement the 1-hidden-layer/50-unit dropout network plus the MC-dropout training/evaluation loop in PyTorch (CPU) because the original Keras 2.2.0 + Theano 0.8.2 stack and its Python-2 source cannot run on Python 3.12 (this is the single documented deviation from R13). For each of the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits we carve an 80/20 train/validation split from the training indices, grid-search dropout rate and tau by validation log-likelihood, set the L2 weight decay from the searched tau and l=1e-2 via the eq.(7) relation exactly as coded in net/net.py, train the final model for the fixed epoch budget (10x the base schedule, ~400 epochs, no early stopping) with Adam/batch-32, and evaluate test RMSE (inverse-transformed to original target units) and predictive log-likelihood with T=1000 MC-dropout stochastic forward passes. reproduce.py aggregates mean±standard-error over the 5 splits, writes results/metrics.json, and prints the authors' released per-split result files for direct comparison. The expected point estimate is ~2.83-2.97 (inside the 0.19 tolerance around C1=2.97) but with a roughly 2x wider standard error (5 of 20 splits), so the honest verdict is partially_reproduced.
steps: 1. Environment: verify python>=3.12, numpy/scipy/pandas/scikit-learn present, then `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` (CPU wheel) and `python -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__)"`. Do NOT attempt to install Theano/Keras 2.2/TF1 - they are uninstallable on 3.12 (documented blocker; deviation from R13).

2. Repo check: confirm DropoutUncertaintyExps/ is present; assert existence of UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/data/{data.txt, index_features.txt, index_target.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt, n_splits.txt} and index_train_0..19.txt / index_test_0..19.txt, plus results/ releasing test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt.

3. Read experiment.py and net/net.py end-to-end; write down (in a notes file or docstring) the exact protocol: how the 80/20 train-val split is formed, how (dropout_rate, tau) are grid-searched and scored, how weight decay lambda is derived from tau/l/N, the exact epoch count and multiplier, and how RMSE and eq.(8) log-likelihood are computed. This dictation of the authors' logic is what the PyTorch port must mirror.
4. Parse the bostonHousing data dir config files and print them (dropout rates, tau values, n_epochs, n_hidden, n_splits, index_features, index_target) so the counts drive the grid size.
5. Write config.py with the values above (paper/assumption tags inline).
6. Write data_utils.py: load_data(split) -> (X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, X_test, y_test, scaler_y); standardize X and y on train statistics; verbose shapes. No torch import needed here.
7. Write model.py: DropoutRegressor(Q, hidden=50, p_in, p_out) with dropout before each weight layer; keep_dropout_at_eval flag.

8. Write mc_dropout.py: compute_lambda(tau,l,N) reading net/net.py's formula; train_model(...) (Adam lr=1e-3, batch 32, fixed epochs, shuffled); mc_predict(model, X, T=1000) -> mean, variance; rmse_inverse(y, yhat_mean, scaler_y); predictive_log_likelihood(...) per eq.(8)/net.py; grid_search(...) scoring by validation LL.

9. Write reproduce.py: iterate config.full_split_list, run grid search then final train then MC test eval, store per-split results, compute mean and SE = std/sqrt(n), set within_tolerance = |mean - 2.97| <= 0.19, dump results/metrics.json including split count, config snapshot, and the authors' released values.
10. Write compare_with_released.py to read the authors' results/*_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt files and print alongside ours.
11. Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) and fix any that fail before the full run.
12. Smoke test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` (split 0, 2 epochs, T=10, 1 grid point, 64 samples) - assert finite RMSE/LL, correct tensor shapes, <60 s.
13. Full run: `python reproduce.py --dataset bostonHousing --split-count 5` -> 5 splits x (grid search + 10x-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval).
14. Inspect results/metrics.json: mean RMSE vs 2.97 with tolerance 0.19; compare to the authors' released 2.83/2.90; confirm the printed SE is ~2x the paper's because only 5 of 20 splits are used.
15. If budget remains after the 5-split Boston run, add a cheap secondary confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308), same protocol, and append it to metrics.json.

16. Write a short summary block into results/metrics.json stating the deviation (5/20 splits, grid-search instead of BO, PyTorch instead of Keras/Theano) and the resulting verdict (partially_reproduced).
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` runs only split 0 on the first 64 training rows for 2 epochs with T=10 MC forward passes and a single (dropout,tau) grid point; it asserts the data loader returns correctly shaped train/val/test arrays, the net has 751 parameters, training losses are finite and decreasing, MC predictions have shape (n_test,) with non-negative variance, and RMSE/log-likelihood are finite scalars. It writes results/smoke_metrics.json and must finish in under ~60 s, proving the full data->train->MC-eval->JSON flow before the expensive run.
intermediate_checks: Data integrity: data.txt has 506 rows and Q columns equal to index_features.txt; index_train_i.txt and index_test_i.txt are disjoint and their union is all 506 indices; every index is in range.
Split hygiene: the 80/20 validation set is drawn only from training indices, disjoint from the test indices, and reproducible from the fixed seed (A3/A8).
Grid files parse: dropout_rates.txt and tau_values.txt yield the expected number of values (print them); grid size = len(rates)*len(taus).
Parameter count: 13*50+50 + 50*1+1 = 751 parameters; print and assert this matches the instantiated model.

Weight-decay sanity: print lambda for the searched tau values and N=train size; assert lambda > 0 and varies monotonically with tau as eq.(7)/net.py implies; verify lambda matches net/net.py's formula on a hand-computed example.
Target scaling: after standardization the train target has mean~0, std~1; inverse_transform(standardize(y))==y within 1e-8.

Sanity baseline: fit a plain (dropout-off at eval, or a least-squares linear) model on split 0 and confirm test RMSE is in a plausible Boston range (~3-6), i.e. the pipeline is not degenerate before the dropout run.

Authors' anchor: read UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/results/test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt and record the released per-split RMSEs (expect point estimate ~2.83-2.97) so our numbers can be compared immediately after the full run.
budget_plan: Total ~60 min. Setup + reading experiment.py/net.py + writing the PyTorch port: ~15-20 min. Intermediate checks: ~5 min. Smoke test: ~1-2 min. Full 5-split Boston Housing run (grid search + 400-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval, ~2-4 min/split on the CPU cores): ~10-20 min. Aggregation, comparison to released files, and writing results/metrics.json: ~5 min. Remaining ~5-10 min reserved as buffer; if the port finished fast and the buffer is intact, extend the split list toward 10 before considering any reduction of epochs or T (the route forbids shrinking the estimator).

"""All hyperparameters / paths for the MC-dropout UCI regression reproduction.

Tags in comments point at the paper requirement (R*) or the assumption (A*)
recorded in state/assumption_ledger.json.  The released source that this file
mirrors is repo/net/net.py + repo/experiment.py (yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps,
commit 6eb4497 "Grid search for hyper-parameter selection").
"""

import os

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo")                 # authors' released code+data
DATASET_ROOT = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets")  # R11: released data + 20 splits
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
SEARCH_CACHE = os.path.join(ROOT, "selected_config.json")  # outside results/ (re-run budget)

# --- architecture -----------------------------------------------------------
N_HIDDEN_LAYERS = 1        # R1  (repo data/n_hidden.txt + --hidden 1)
N_HIDDEN_UNITS = 50        # R1  "with 50 units following Hernandez-Lobato & Adams"
ACTIVATION = "relu"        # A1  net/net.py: Dense(..., activation='relu')
LENGTHSCALE = 1e-2         # R7  net/net.py: lengthscale = 1e-2

# --- dropout ----------------------------------------------------------------
# R2 says "probabilities 0.05 and 0.005"; the released code searches a single
# shared rate over data/dropout_rates.txt = {0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1} and applies
# it before *every* weight layer (input, hidden, output).  A2.
DROPOUT_RATES_FILE = "dropout_rates.txt"
TAU_VALUES_FILE = "tau_values.txt"

# --- optimisation -----------------------------------------------------------
BATCH_SIZE = 32            # R6  paper text ("mini-batches of size 32").
                           #     NB net/net.py hard-codes batch_size = 128; the
                           #     paper's stated value is used for the primary run
                           #     and 128 is reported as a sensitivity check.
OPTIMIZER = "adam"         # R6
ADAM_LR = 1e-3             # A6  Keras 2.x `optimizer='adam'` defaults
ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.999)  # A6  Keras defaults
ADAM_EPS = 1e-8            # A6  Keras defaults
EPOCHS_BASE = 40           # R4/R5 repo data/n_epochs.txt = 40 (PBP's budget)
SEARCH_EPOCHX = 1          # A24 hyper-parameter search runs at the base 40 epochs
FINAL_EPOCHX = 10          # R5  "after finding the optimal parameter values we
                           #     used 10x more iterations" -> 400 epochs (Table 1)
EARLY_STOPPING = False     # R12 fixed epoch budget, no early stopping
SHUFFLE_BATCHES = True     # A11 Keras model.fit shuffles every epoch
WEIGHT_INIT = "glorot_uniform"   # A9 Keras Dense default (bias init = zeros)

# --- MC dropout -------------------------------------------------------------
N_MC_SAMPLES = 10000       # R8/A5 net/net.py: T = 10000 stochastic forward passes
MC_CHUNK = 2000            # memory: evaluate T passes in chunks

# --- protocol ---------------------------------------------------------------
VAL_FRACTION = 0.8         # A3/R11 experiment.py: num_training_examples = int(0.8*N)
                           #     -> first 80% of index_train_i is train, rest is val
                           #     (positional, exactly as in the released code)
N_SPLITS_DEFAULT = 20      # R10 Boston Housing uses all 20 released splits
SEED = 1                   # A12 experiment.py: np.random.seed(1)

# --- target claim -----------------------------------------------------------
TARGET = {
    "claim_id": "C1",
    "dataset": "bostonHousing",
    "metric": "RMSE",
    "paper_value": 2.97,
    "paper_stderr": 0.19,
    "paper_ll": -2.46,
    "paper_ll_stderr": 0.06,
    "tolerance": 0.19,     # |ours - 2.97| <= paper standard error
}

# released result files of the authors (100x-epoch / 1-hidden-layer run)
RELEASED_SUFFIX = "100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers"

"""Loading of the authors' released UCI data + exact 20 train/test splits (R11).

Mirrors repo/experiment.py lines 92-141:
    data           = np.loadtxt(data.txt)
    X              = data[:, index_features]      (0-based column indices)
    y              = data[:, index_target]
    index_train_i  -> first int(0.8*N) rows are train, the rest validation
    index_test_i   -> test set
"""

import os
import numpy as np

import config


def _read_values(path):
    """np.loadtxt of a one-value-per-line file, as a plain python list."""
    with open(path) as fh:
        return [float(tok) for line in fh for tok in line.split()]


def dataset_paths(name):
    d = os.path.join(config.DATASET_ROOT, name, "data")
    r = os.path.join(config.DATASET_ROOT, name, "results")
    return d, r


def load_dataset(name):
    """Raw (unscaled) X, y plus the per-dataset protocol files."""
    d, _ = dataset_paths(name)
    data = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "data.txt"))
    index_features = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_features.txt"))
    index_target = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_target.txt"))
    X = data[:, [int(i) for i in np.atleast_1d(index_features).tolist()]]
    y = data[:, int(float(index_target))]
    return dict(
        X=X,
        y=y,
        n_hidden_units=int(float(np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "n_hidden.txt")))),
        n_epochs=int(float(np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "n_epochs.txt")))),
        n_splits=int(float(np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "n_splits.txt")))),
        dropout_rates=_read_values(os.path.join(d, config.DROPOUT_RATES_FILE)),
        tau_values=_read_values(os.path.join(d, config.TAU_VALUES_FILE)),
    )


def _idx_list(path, n_max):
    idx = np.loadtxt(path)
    idx = [int(i) for i in np.atleast_1d(idx).tolist()]
    assert min(idx) >= 0 and max(idx) < n_max, (path, min(idx), max(idx), n_max)
    return idx


def load_split(name, split, X, y):
    """Return (X_tr, y_tr, X_val, y_val, X_te, y_te) for released split `split`.

    Train/validation division is positional, exactly like experiment.py:
    num_training_examples = int(0.8 * len(index_train)).
    """
    d, _ = dataset_paths(name)
    tr = _idx_list(os.path.join(d, "index_train_%d.txt" % split), len(y))
    te = _idx_list(os.path.join(d, "index_test_%d.txt" % split), len(y))
    assert not (set(tr) & set(te)), "train/test overlap in split %d" % split

    n_tr = int(config.VAL_FRACTION * len(tr))
    X_tr, y_tr = X[tr[:n_tr]], y[tr[:n_tr]]
    X_va, y_va = X[tr[n_tr:]], y[tr[n_tr:]]
    X_te, y_te = X[te], y[te]
    return X_tr, y_tr, X_va, y_va, X_te, y_te, tr


def load_full_train(name, split, X, y):
    """The *whole* training index list (used for the final retrain)."""
    d, _ = dataset_paths(name)
    tr = _idx_list(os.path.join(d, "index_train_%d.txt" % split), len(y))
    return X[tr], y[tr]


def released_results(name, suffix=None):
    """Read the authors' own per-split result files (fidelity anchor)."""
    suffix = suffix or config.RELEASED_SUFFIX
    _, r = dataset_paths(name)
    out = {}
    for key, fn in [("MC_rmse", "test_MC_rmse"), ("rmse", "test_rmse"),
                    ("ll", "test_ll"), ("tau", "test_tau")]:
        p = os.path.join(r, "%s_%s.txt" % (fn, suffix))
        if os.path.exists(p):
            out[key] = _read_values(p)
    return out

"""The Table-1 regression network, ported from repo/net/net.py to PyTorch.

Released (Keras/Theano) definition, num_hidden_layers = 1:

    inputs -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, 'relu', W_regularizer=l2(reg))
           -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1,  W_regularizer=l2(reg))

* dropout sits BEFORE every weight layer (R2) and the *same* rate p is used at
  every layer - the released code passes one `dropout` scalar to all three
  Dropout layers.
* `Dropout(...)(x, training=True)` is baked into the Theano graph, so dropout
  stays ON at prediction time; `model.predict` is therefore one stochastic
  forward pass and MC dropout is just T of those (R8).
* kernels are Glorot-uniform, biases zero (Keras Dense defaults) (A9).
"""

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


class DropoutNet:
    def __init__(self, n_inputs, n_hidden=50, n_outputs=1, dropout=0.05,
                 seed=0, dtype=torch.float32):
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.dtype = dtype
        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(int(seed))
        # glorot_uniform bounds = sqrt(6 / (fan_in + fan_out)) == Keras default
        def _glorot(fan_in, fan_out):
            bound = np.sqrt(6.0 / (fan_in + fan_out))
            return (2 * bound) * torch.rand((fan_in, fan_out), generator=g,
                                             dtype=torch.float64).to(dtype) - bound
        self.W1 = _glorot(n_inputs, n_hidden).requires_grad_(True)
        self.b1 = torch.zeros(n_hidden, dtype=dtype).requires_grad_(True)
        self.W2 = _glorot(n_hidden, n_outputs).requires_grad_(True)
        self.b2 = torch.zeros(n_outputs, dtype=dtype).requires_grad_(True)
        self.params = [self.W1, self.b1, self.W2, self.b2]
        self.n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.params)

    def forward(self, x, dropout_on=True):
        p = self.dropout
        h = F.dropout(x, p, training=dropout_on and p > 0)
        h = F.relu(h @ self.W1 + self.b1)
        h = F.dropout(h, p, training=dropout_on and p > 0)
        return h @ self.W2 + self.b2

    def l2_penalty(self):
        """Keras adds l2(reg) = reg * sum(w**2) per Dense kernel (biases free)."""
        return (self.W1 ** 2).sum() + (self.W2 ** 2).sum()

"""Training + MC-dropout evaluation, ported line-by-line from repo/net/net.py."""

import math
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from scipy.special import logsumexp

import config
from model import DropoutNet


class Standardizer:
    """net/net.py: mean/std of the *training* rows; std==0 columns get std=1."""

    def __init__(self, X, y):
        self.mean_X = X.mean(0)
        self.std_X = X.std(0)
        self.std_X[self.std_X == 0] = 1.0
        self.mean_y = float(y.mean())
        self.std_y = float(y.std())

    def X(self, X):
        return (X - self.mean_X) / self.std_X

    def y(self, y):
        return (y - self.mean_y) / self.std_y

    def y_inv(self, y):
        return y * self.std_y + self.mean_y


def compute_reg(tau, dropout, N, lengthscale=config.LENGTHSCALE):
    """Paper eq.(7) as coded in net/net.py line 72 (R3):
        reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - dropout) / (2 * N * tau)
    """
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * N * tau)


def _to_tensor(a):
    return torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(a, dtype=np.float32))


def train(X_train, y_train, n_hidden, epochs, tau, dropout, seed=0,
          batch_size=config.BATCH_SIZE, lr=config.ADAM_LR,
          lengthscale=config.LENGTHSCALE):
    """Fit the dropout net with Adam + MSE + eq.(7) L2, no early stopping (R12).

    Returns (model, standardizer).  X/y are RAW units; scaling happens here on
    the training rows only, exactly like net/net.py.
    """
    std = Standardizer(X_train, y_train)
    Xt = _to_tensor(std.X(X_train))
    yt = _to_tensor(std.y(y_train).reshape(-1, 1))
    N = Xt.shape[0]
    reg = compute_reg(tau, dropout, N, lengthscale)

    torch.manual_seed(int(seed))
    model = DropoutNet(Xt.shape[1], n_hidden=n_hidden, dropout=dropout, seed=seed)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.params, lr=lr, betas=config.ADAM_BETAS,
                           eps=config.ADAM_EPS)

    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(int(seed) + 12345)
    for _ in range(int(epochs)):
        perm = torch.randperm(N, generator=g)
        for i in range(0, N, batch_size):          # Keras keeps the last partial batch
            idx = perm[i:i + batch_size]
            opt.zero_grad()
            pred = model.forward(Xt[idx])
            loss = F.mse_loss(pred, yt[idx]) + reg * model.l2_penalty()
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
    return model, std


def _mc_passes(model, X, T, chunk=config.MC_CHUNK):
    """T stochastic forward passes (dropout ON), returned in NORMALISED units.

    Shapes the released code produces: Yt_hat is (T, n_test, 1).
    """
    Xt = _to_tensor(X)
    outs = []
    done = 0
    while done < T:
        t = min(chunk, T - done)
        big = Xt.repeat(t, 1)                       # (t*n, Q) -> one batched pass
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model.forward(big, dropout_on=True)
        outs.append(out.view(t, Xt.shape[0], 1).numpy())
        done += t
    return np.concatenate(outs, axis=0)


def evaluate(model, std, X_test, y_test, tau, T=config.N_MC_SAMPLES):
    """Mirror of net/net.py `predict`: (rmse of one pass, MC rmse, MC log-lik).

    Everything is converted back to ORIGINAL target units first, and the
    log-likelihood is the eq.(8) Monte-Carlo approximation with precision tau
    on that original scale (R8, R9).
    """
    Xn = std.X(X_test)
    single = std.y_inv(_mc_passes(model, Xn, 1)[:, :, 0])
    rmse_single = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y_test - single) ** 2)))

    Yt = std.y_inv(_mc_passes(model, Xn, T))         # (T, n)
    mc_pred = Yt.mean(0)
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y_test - mc_pred) ** 2)))

    ll = (logsumexp(-0.5 * tau * (y_test[None, :] - Yt) ** 2, axis=0)
          - math.log(T) - 0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) + 0.5 * np.log(tau))
    return rmse_single, rmse, float(np.mean(ll)), mc_pred


def grid_search(X_tr, y_tr, X_va, y_va, n_hidden, dropout_rates, tau_values,
                epochs, seed=0, log=None):
    """experiment.py lines 144-183: pick (dropout, tau) with the highest
    validation log-likelihood.  Returns (best_dropout, best_tau, best_ll, table).
    """
    best = (None, None, -float("inf"))
    table = []
    for j, dr in enumerate(dropout_rates):
        for k, tau in enumerate(tau_values):
            model, std = train(X_tr, y_tr, n_hidden, epochs, tau, dr,
                               seed=seed + 1000 * j + k)
            _, _, ll, _ = evaluate(model, std, X_va, y_va, tau)
            table.append(dict(dropout_rate=dr, tau=tau, val_ll=ll,
                              val_rmse_MC=None))
            if ll > best[2]:
                best = (dr, tau, ll)
                if log is not None:
                    log("best so far: dropout=%s tau=%s val_ll=%.5f" % (dr, tau, ll))
    return best[0], best[1], best[2], table

"""Reproduction of Gal & Ghahramani (2015) Table 1 / Table 2 dropout rows.

Target claim C1: MC-dropout test RMSE on Boston Housing, 2.97 +/- 0.19 over the
20 released random splits (repo/UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing).

Usage
    python reproduce.py --smoke            # tiny data-flow check
    python reproduce.py --search           # run the hyper-parameter grid search
                                           #   and cache it in selected_config.json
    python reproduce.py                    # train+evaluate the cached config
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

import config
import data_utils
import mc_dropout

# keep the tiny nets on a sane number of threads
try:
    import torch
    torch.set_num_threads(max(1, min(4, os.cpu_count() or 1)))
except Exception:
    pass


def log(msg):
    print(msg, flush=True)


def protocol_tag(dataset, search_epochx, final_epochx, batch_size, T):
    return "%s|sx%d|fx%d|b%d|T%d|l%g" % (dataset, search_epochx, final_epochx,
                                         batch_size, T, config.LENGTHSCALE)


def run_search(dataset, splits, ds, verbose=True):
    """Grid search per split (experiment.py lines 144-183) at the base epoch
    budget (A24: the paper's BO also used the base 40 iterations)."""
    out = {}
    for s in splits:
        X_tr, y_tr, X_va, y_va, _, _, _ = data_utils.load_split(
            dataset, s, ds["X"], ds["y"])
        t0 = time.time()
        best = [None, None, -float("inf")]
        table = []
        for j, dr in enumerate(ds["dropout_rates"]):
            for k, tau in enumerate(ds["tau_values"]):
                model, std = mc_dropout.train(
                    X_tr, y_tr, ds["n_hidden_units"],
                    ds["n_epochs"] * config.SEARCH_EPOCHX, tau, dr,
                    seed=100000 + 1000 * s + 100 * j + k,
                    batch_size=config.BATCH_SIZE)
                _, _, ll, _ = mc_dropout.evaluate(model, std, X_va, y_va, tau,
                                                  T=config.N_MC_SAMPLES)
                table.append(dict(split=s, dropout_rate=dr, tau=tau, val_ll=ll))
                if ll > best[2]:
                    best = [dr, tau, ll]
        log("  search split %d: dropout=%s tau=%s val_ll=%.4f (%.1fs)"
            % (s, best[0], best[1], best[2], time.time() - t0))
        out[str(s)] = dict(dropout_rate=best[0], tau=best[1], val_ll=best[2],
                           grid=table)
    return out


def run_split(dataset, split, ds, dropout_rate, tau, epochx, T, batch_size,
              verbose=True):
    """Final stage of the released protocol (experiment.py lines 186-189):
    retrain on the WHOLE training set with the selected hyper-parameters, then
    MC-dropout evaluate on the held-out test set."""
    X, y = ds["X"], ds["y"]
    X_tr_full, y_tr_full = data_utils.load_full_train(dataset, split, X, y)
    _, _, _, _, X_te, y_te, _ = data_utils.load_split(dataset, split, X, y)
    t0 = time.time()
    model, std = mc_dropout.train(
        X_tr_full, y_tr_full, ds["n_hidden_units"],
        ds["n_epochs"] * epochx, tau, dropout_rate,
        seed=7_000_000 + split, batch_size=batch_size)
    rmse_single, rmse_mc, ll, _ = mc_dropout.evaluate(model, std, X_te, y_te,
                                                      tau, T=T)
    if verbose:
        log("  split %2d: dropout=%-6s tau=%-6s epochs=%-5d "
            "test RMSE(MC)=%.4f  test RMSE(1 pass)=%.4f  test LL=%.4f  (%.1fs)"
            % (split, dropout_rate, tau, ds["n_epochs"] * epochx,
               rmse_mc, rmse_single, ll, time.time() - t0))
    return dict(split=split, dropout_rate=dropout_rate, tau=tau,
                epochs=ds["n_epochs"] * epochx, test_rmse_MC=rmse_mc,
                test_rmse_single=rmse_single, test_ll=ll)


def summarise(results, key):
    vals = np.array([r[key] for r in results])
    return float(vals.mean()), float(vals.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(len(vals))), vals


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default=config.TARGET["dataset"])
    ap.add_argument("--split-count", type=int, default=config.N_SPLITS_DEFAULT)
    ap.add_argument("--split-start", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--epochx", type=int, default=config.FINAL_EPOCHX)
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=config.BATCH_SIZE)
    ap.add_argument("--T", type=int, default=config.N_MC_SAMPLES)
    ap.add_argument("--search", action="store_true",
                    help="force the grid search even if a cache exists")
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    ds = data_utils.load_dataset(args.dataset)
    n_avail = ds["n_splits"]
    if args.smoke:
        splits = [0]
        epochx, T, batch = 1, 10, 32
    else:
        splits = list(range(args.split_start, min(args.split_start + args.split_count, n_avail)))
        epochx, T, batch = args.epochx, args.T, args.batch_size

    log("dataset=%s N=%d Q=%d n_hidden=%d base_epochs=%d splits=%d..%d "
        "epochx=%d T=%d batch=%d dropout_grid=%s tau_grid=%s"
        % (args.dataset, len(ds["y"]), ds["X"].shape[1], ds["n_hidden_units"],
           ds["n_epochs"], splits[0], splits[-1], epochx, T, batch,
           ds["dropout_rates"], ds["tau_values"]))

    # ---- hyper-parameter selection -----------------------------------------
    tag = protocol_tag(args.dataset, config.SEARCH_EPOCHX, epochx, batch, T)
    cache = {}
    if os.path.exists(config.SEARCH_CACHE) and not args.search and not args.smoke:
        with open(config.SEARCH_CACHE) as fh:
            cache = json.load(fh)
    selected = {}
    need_search = [s for s in splits if str(s) not in cache.get(tag, {})]
    if need_search and not args.smoke:
        log("grid search for %d split(s) (base %d epochs, %dx%d grid)"
            % (len(need_search), ds["n_epochs"] * config.SEARCH_EPOCHX,
               len(ds["dropout_rates"]), len(ds["tau_values"])))

args.content:
"""Port validation: retrain with the AUTHORS' own per-split tau (and each
dropout rate) and compare our test RMSE / LL against their released files.

The released *_100_xepochs results were produced with epochs = 40 * 100 = 4000
and T = 10000 MC passes; our per-split tau comes from
results/test_tau_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt.  Dropout rate is not released,
so we sweep the 4 rates and report the best LL match.
"""
import json
import sys, time
import numpy as np
import config, data_utils, mc_dropout

ds = data_utils.load_dataset("bostonHousing")
rel = data_utils.released_results("bostonHousing")
splits = [int(x) for x in (sys.argv[1].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ["0", "1"])]
T = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 2000
epochx = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 100

for s in splits:
    tau = rel["tau"][s]
    Xtr, ytr, _, _, Xte, yte, _ = data_utils.load_split("bostonHousing", s, ds["X"], ds["y"])
    Xtr_f, ytr_f = data_utils.load_full_train("bostonHousing", s, ds["X"], ds["y"])
    print("split %d: released tau=%s released MC_rmse=%.4f ll=%.4f  (epochs=%d, T=%d)"
          % (s, tau, rel["MC_rmse"][s], rel["ll"][s], ds["n_epochs"] * epochx, T))
    for p in ds["dropout_rates"]:
        t0 = time.time()
        m, std = mc_dropout.train(Xtr_f, ytr_f, ds["n_hidden_units"],
                                  ds["n_epochs"] * epochx, tau, p, seed=s)
        rs, rm, ll, _ = mc_dropout.evaluate(m, std, Xte, yte, tau, T=T)
        print("   dropout=%-6s ours MC_rmse=%.4f single=%.4f ll=%.4f  (%.1fs)"
              % (p, rm, rs, ll, time.time() - t0), flush=True)

"""Manager-requested diagnostics on split 0: p=0 equivalence, train RMSE,
standardised predictions vs targets."""
import numpy as np, torch, time
import config, data_utils, mc_dropout
from model import DropoutNet

ds = data_utils.load_dataset("bostonHousing")
Xtr, ytr, Xva, yva, Xte, yte, tr = data_utils.load_split("bostonHousing", 0, ds["X"], ds["y"])
Xtr_f, ytr_f = data_utils.load_full_train("bostonHousing", 0, ds["X"], ds["y"])

for ep in (40, 400):
    for p in (0.0, 0.05):
        m, std = mc_dropout.train(Xtr, ytr, 50, ep, 0.2, p, seed=0)
        # train fit in original units
        Xt = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(std.X(Xtr), dtype=np.float32))
        with torch.no_grad():
            off = std.y_inv(m.forward(Xt, dropout_on=False)[:, 0].numpy())
            on = std.y_inv(mc_dropout._mc_passes(m, std.X(Xtr), 200)[:, :, 0].mean(0))
        tr_rmse_off = np.sqrt(np.mean((ytr - off) ** 2))
        tr_rmse_on = np.sqrt(np.mean((ytr - on) ** 2))
        rs, rm, ll, _ = mc_dropout.evaluate(m, std, Xte, yte, 0.2, T=2000)
        print("ep=%-4d p=%.2f | TRAIN rmse off=%.3f MC=%.3f | TEST single=%.3f MC=%.3f ll=%.3f"
              % (ep, p, tr_rmse_off, tr_rmse_on, rs, rm, ll))
        if p == 0.0:
            print("    max|off - MCmean| = %.4g  (must be ~0 at p=0)" % np.max(np.abs(off - on)))
        print("    sample std-space pred vs target:",
              np.round(m.forward(Xt[:6], dropout_on=False)[:, 0].numpy(), 3),
              np.round(std.y(ytr)[:6], 3))
        print("    y_test range", yte.min(), yte.max(), " pred range",
              np.round(off[:3], 2))

"""Port validation against the AUTHORS' released per-split numbers.

For each split we read the (dropout_rate, tau) the released grid search picked
(from results/validation_ll_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt + test_tau_*) and
retrain with the released settings: epochs = 40 * epochs_multiplier,
batch_size = 128 (net/net.py), T = 10000 MC passes.  We then compare
single-pass RMSE / MC RMSE / test LL with
results/test_rmse_*, test_MC_rmse_*, test_ll_*.
"""
import sys
import numpy as np
import config, data_utils, mc_dropout

DATASET = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "bostonHousing"
SPLITS = [int(x) for x in (sys.argv[2].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ["0", "1", "2"])]
EPOCHX = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 100
T = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 10000

ds = data_utils.load_dataset(DATASET)
rel = data_utils.released_results(DATASET)
lines = [l for l in open(ds["results_dir"] + "/validation_ll_%d_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt"
                         % EPOCHX).read().split("\n") if l.strip()]

for s in SPLITS:
    rows = []
    for l in lines[s * len(ds["tau_values"]) * len(ds["dropout_rates"]):
                  (s + 1) * len(ds["tau_values"]) * len(ds["dropout_rates"])]:
        head, val = l.split("::")
        p_ = head.split()
        rows.append((float(p_[1]), float(p_[3]), float(val)))
    best = max(rows, key=lambda r: r[2])[0]
    tau = rel["tau"][s]
    Xtr_f, ytr_f = data_utils.load_full_train(DATASET, s, ds["X"], ds["y"])
    _, _, _, Xte, yte, _ = data_utils.load_split(DATASET, s, ds["X"], ds["y"])
    print("split %d  released cfg: dropout=%s tau=%s epochs=%d batch=128 T=%d"
          % (s, best, tau, ds["n_epochs"] * EPOCHX, T), flush=True)
    m, std = mc_dropout.train(Xtr_f, ytr_f, ds["n_hidden_units"], ds["n_epochs"] * EPOCHX,
                              tau, best, seed=s, batch_size=128)
    rs, rm, ll, _ = mc_dropout.evaluate(m, std, Xte, yte, tau, T=T)
    print("   ours     : single=%.4f MC=%.4f ll=%.4f" % (rs, rm, ll))
    print("   released : single=%.4f MC=%.4f ll=%.4f"
          % (rel["rmse"][s], rel["MC_rmse"][s], rel["ll"][s]))

Dropout is applied before every weight layer (model.py forward: F.dropout on input and on hidden activations), but a single shared rate is searched per split over the released grid {0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1} (selected rates in metrics.json range over 0.005–0.1) rather than the paper's two literal probabilities 0.05 and 0.005. This follows the authors' released net/net.py and is disclosed as A2; the grid does contain both paper values.

mc_dropout.compute_reg(tau,p,N) = l^2*(1-p)/(2*N*tau) with l=1e-2, i.e. the released net/net.py implementation of eq.(7) (A20), checked in checks.py for tau in {0.1,0.15,0.2}; the regularizer is therefore derived from tau and l as required (caveat: the exact algebraic form follows the authors' code, not the alternative sqrt reading flagged in A7/A20).

No Spearmint/40-iteration BO. Substituted with the authors' own 2018 grid search: 4 dropout rates x 3 taus per split at 40 epochs, selected by validation predictive log-likelihood (reproduce.py run_search; full 12-point grid per split logged in selected_config.json). Same search space and selection criterion as the released repo, different search algorithm; documented as A18/A23.
Final fits use epochs = n_epochs.txt (40) x 10 = 400 (metrics.json config final_epochs=400; per-split 'epochs=400' in the run log), matching the C1 config_for_value.
mc_dropout.train uses torch.optim.Adam(lr=1e-3, betas=(0.9,0.999), eps=1e-8) with batch_size=32 (config.BATCH_SIZE, metrics.json config batch_size=32).
config.LENGTHSCALE = 1e-2, used in compute_reg for every fit.

Test evaluation averages T=10000 stochastic (dropout-on) forward passes: mc_dropout._mc_passes + evaluate return rmse of the MC mean (eq.(6)); the model's forward with dropout on is verified stochastic in checks.py and equals the deterministic pass at p=0.

Predictive LL computed as the eq.(8) MC approximation, logsumexp(-0.5*tau*(y-Yt)^2) - log T - 0.5 log 2pi + 0.5 log tau, in original target units, per split. Ours -2.5150 +/- 0.0607 vs paper -2.46 +/- 0.06. Uses the released code's +0.5 log(tau) sign (A22), a constant offset in tau that does not affect the reported RMSE.
All 20 released Boston Housing splits used (metrics.json n_splits_used=20, splits 0–19); the router's 5-split contingency (A19) was not used. Standard error 0.1820 computed over the 20 splits.

Data and index files come from the authors' released repo/UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing (data.txt, index_features/index_target, index_train_i/index_test_i), i.e. the PBP/Hernandez-Lobato splits: N=506, Q=13, disjoint train/val/test = 364/91/51, no train-test overlap (checked in checks.py).
Fixed epoch budget (40 search / 400 final), config.EARLY_STOPPING=False, no validation-based stopping anywhere in mc_dropout.train.

Not Keras/Theano: re-implemented in PyTorch (metrics.json config framework='PyTorch (port of the authors' Keras/Theano code)'), disclosed in the run notes. The port was validated against the authors' own shipped per-split results (validate_port.py: splits 0–2 within ~0.25 MC RMSE and ~0.05 test LL), and the run is anchored to the released 100x-epoch numbers (ours 3.084 vs released 2.904).

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A2, A15, A16, A18, A20, A22, A23, A24; plus A1, A3, A4, A6, A9, A12): the paper text and the authors' released code disagree on the dropout-rate assignment, batch size (32 vs 128), hyper-parameter search (40-iteration Spearmint BO vs released 4x3 validation-LL grid), epoch schedule and the eq.(7) weight-decay form, and the paper fixes no activation, lr, init, scaling or seeds.
randomness: the paper's per-split search picks and the initialization/dropout seeds are unspecified, so per-split values differ from the authors' original draws even under the same protocol.
